svg.title: The input gradient sums contributions from every neuron the input feeds
svg.desc: Two hand-drawn panels over the same three-neuron layer, differing only in how many paths are lit. In the left panel a weight has one path: W one one reaches the loss through Z one and nothing else, so its gradient is the plain product of the upstream at Z one and the input, and the other two routes are drawn faint. In the right panel an input has every path: X one reaches the loss through all three neurons via W one one, W two one and W three one, so its gradient is a sum of three terms, one per neuron. A band gives the matrix form, the input gradient equals the upstream gradient dotted with W, with shapes one by m dotted with m by n giving one by n, and notes that the contracted dimension m is the neuron count, exactly the paths the sum has to run over.
svg.text: A weight touches one neuron. An input touches all of them, and the chain rule sums over every route it takes.
W₁₁ reaches the loss through Z₁ and nothing else
One term, so the chain rule reads as a plain product.
X₁ reaches the loss through all three neurons
Three terms, one per neuron. The sum is not optional.
The contracted dimension is m, the neuron count: exactly the paths the sum has to run over.
